title: DLMF 1.10 Functions of a Complex Variable: Let f(z) be analytic on the disk \left|z-z_{0}\right|<R .
summary: DLMF 1.10 Functions of a Complex Variable: Let f(z) be analytic on the disk \left|z-z_{0}\right|<R .
body: NIST DLMF section 1.10 (Functions of a Complex Variable) says: "Let f(z) be analytic on the disk \left|z-z_{0}\right|<R . Then The right-hand side is the Taylor series for f(z) at z=z_{0} , and its radius of convergence is at least R . Note that ( 1.10.4 ) is a generalization of the binomial expansion ( 1.2.2 ) with the binomial coefficients defined in ( 1.2.6 ). Again, in these examples \ln\left(1+z\right) and (1-z)^{-\alpha} have their principal values; see §§ 4.2(i) and 4.2(iv) . An analytic function f(z) has a zero of order (or multiplicity ) m ( \geq\!1 ) at z_{0} if the first nonzero coefficient in its Taylor series at z_{0} is that of (z-z_{0})^{m} . When m=1 the zero is simple . Let f_{1}(z) be analytic in a domain D_{1} . If f_{2}(z) , analytic in D_{2} , equals f_{1}(z) on an arc in D=D_{1}\cap D_{2} , or on just an infinite number of points with a limit point in D , then they are equal throughout D and f_{2}(z) is called an analytic continuation of f_{1}(z) . We write (f_{1},D_{1}) , (f_{2},D_{2}) to signify this continuation." Equation 1.10.1 on the page has alt text "f(z)=\sum^{\infty}_{n=0}\frac{f^{(n)}(z_{0})}{n!}(z-z_{0})^{n}.". Equation 1.10.2 on the page has alt text "{\mathrm{e}}^{z}=1+\frac{z}{1!}+\frac{z^{2}}{2!}+\cdots,". This card records that section's wording and equation alt text. It does not retypeset a formula the alt text did not carry.
